content:
I checked all 14 listed outputs; they match the stated LSB-based interleaving. The indexing/zero-padding clarification raised by User123 and the formatting/stub changes requested by 5DN1L appear addressed.

One small coverage gap remains: Test 2 exercises A=B=0, but Validator 2 uses A=B=1, and no other validator expects M=0. Please preserve the all-zero boundary in the hidden suite as well. A solution that forgets to output zero could currently pass every validator. Here the only input for that boundary is 0 0, so an identical test/validator pair is justified; there is no need to invent different data that change the scenario.

My comparison with accepted bit-manipulation tasks did not identify the same two-integer bit-interleaving rule. That is a bounded search result, not proof of novelty.

"Bit i of A/B" (e.g., A0) refers to the i-th (zero-indexed) LSB of A/B, but "bit i of M" (e.g., M0) refers to the i-th (zero-indexed) MSB of M. This creates a bit (no pun intended) of confusion in the statement "bit i of A becomes bit 2·i of M". Please edit this accordingly.

Please also state that, if A/B has less bits than the other, their bit representation should first be left-padded with zeros (e.g. from your example: 3 -> 11₂ -> 011₂).

Thank you :)
I hope you received enough feedback from the community to improve your contribution. Once you have made the necessary updates, publish your contribution!

Goal
* Please format "A", "B", "M", "i", "A0", "B0", "A1", "B1", "A2" and "B2" as [[variables]] instead of in <<bold>>.

* Please exclude "2·" and "+ 1" from [[variable]] formatting.

* Please change "(bit 0)" to "(LSB, i.e. bit 0)".

Input
* Please format "A" and "B" as [[variables]] instead of in <<bold>>.

Output
* Please format "M" as a [[variable]] instead of in <<bold>>.

Constraints
* Please format only "A" and "B" as [[variables]], and exclude the rest of the inequalities from [[variable]] formatting.

Stub generator
* Please add a write statement before STATEMENT, e.g. "write answer".

Cases
* Please add a new pair of cases where [[A]] is a 2-digit integer and [[B]] is a 4-digit integer.

* Please add a new pair of cases where [[A]] is a 4-digit integer and [[B]] is a 2-digit integer.

* Please add a new pair of cases where both [[A]] and [[B]] are 3-digit integers and [[A]] < [[B]].

Thanks.
If I'm not mistaken, the guidelines say that input variables, like A and B in both Goal and Input, should be formatted as {{variable}}.
Square brackets instead of curly ones. 😉

Thanks a lot for the feedback.
It was very helpful and clear.
I’ve updated the statement, formatting, stub, and test cases accordingly.

Thanks :) I updated the statement to make it clearer and added the zero-padding part.

Just one thing: M0 is still the LSB, not the MSB. The confusion was just because binary numbers are normally written MSB first.
Thank you for updating the contribution too! I don't have any further comments for now.
